# Purpose and use

Reproducible source of the statistics, tables and figures for the manuscript on soft rot *Pectobacteriaceae* (SRP) in Montana seed potato, 2024-2026. The file cleans the input workbooks, runs the analyses and writes every figure (PNG, PDF, SVG) and table (CSV) to `outputs/`.

**To run**

1. Input files are read from one folder, set by `data_dir` (chunk `data-dir`) or the environment variable `SRP_DATA_DIR`. Required: the workbooks listed in that chunk and `name_crosswalks.csv` (grower name mappings). Optional (the matching figure or check is skipped when absent): `mashtree_ALL_bootstrap.nwk` (Figure 9), `mashtree_ALL_distances.tsv` (Figure S8) and `fastani_allvsall.tsv` (marks mixed assemblies in Figures 9 and S8), `isolate_decay.xlsx` (Figure 13), `effector_candidates_25.xlsx`, `Table2_isolate_source_qpcr_pitting.csv`, `Table4_isolate_ani_taxonomy_source.csv`.
2. Knit the file. Output: `outputs/figures/`, `outputs/tables/`, `outputs/all_tables_combined.xlsx`, `outputs/analysis_objects.rds`.

Besides Figures 1-13 and S1-S8, the file draws the sample summary (`Fig_sample_summary`) and two isolate figures (`Fig_isolate_source_qpcr_pitting`, `Fig_isolate_ani_taxonomy`).

| Figure | Content | File stem |
|:--|:----------------------------------------|:------------------------------|
| 1 | Prevalence by target: (A) plants tested, 2024-2026; (B) environmental sites (air, irrigation water), 2025-2026 | `Fig1_prevalence_plant_environment` |
| 2 | Prevalence by seed generation | `Fig2_prevalence_by_generation` |
| 3 | Prevalence by region | `Fig3_prevalence_by_region` |
| 4 | Co-occurrence (Jaccard) and genus classes, plants tested | `Fig4_cooccurrence_three_seasons` |
| 5 | Prevalence by variety (2025-2026) | `Fig5_prevalence_by_variety` |
| 6 | Maps of sampled locations | `Fig6_maps_locations` |
| 7 | Not drawn (merged into Figure 1B; the Gallatin Valley comparison is a table only) | - |
| 8 | Isolates: ANI and decayed tissue weight | `Fig8_isolates_ANI_decay` |
| 9 | Mashtree tree of all isolates and references, with bootstrap support, species groups, closest species by ANI, reported ANI, source and pitting on CVP agar | `Fig9_mashtree_all_isolates` |
| 10 | Pectin-like and hemicellulose-like PCWDE gene counts, T5aSS and pitting on CVP agar against decayed tissue weight | `Fig10_pcwde_t5ass_pitting_vs_decay` |
| 11 | Correlation of those features with decayed tissue weight, ANI and pitting | `Fig11_feature_correlations` |
| 12 | All genome features of the sequenced isolates: secretion systems, pilus, flagellum, CAZymes and PCWDE, effector candidate, mobile elements | `Fig12_genome_feature_matrix` |
| 13 | Decayed tissue weight (mean and SD) of each isolate by sample type, with the pathogenic call | `Fig13_isolate_decay_by_sample_type` |
| S1 | Sample-level sensitivity analysis, plant-level odds ratios (GEE) and plants tested per sample | `S1_sample_level_sensitivity` |
| S2 | 2026 plant-level co-occurrence | `S2_plant_level_2026_cooccurrence` |
| S3 | Detection probability versus stems tested | `S3_detection_probability_vs_stems` |
| S4 | Sample by target detection matrix | `S4_detection_matrix` |
| S5 | Environmental sampling effort, locations, replicates | `S5_environmental_detail` |
| S6 | Decayed tissue weight per isolate | `S6_isolate_decay_per_isolate` |
| S7 | Genomic features of each sequenced isolate, ordered by decayed tissue weight | `S7_genomic_features_per_isolate` |
| S8 | Mash distances among the reference genomes and the sequenced isolates (heatmaps) | `S8_mash_distance_heatmap` |

**Table 1** (plants tested, SRP-positive and SRP-negative plants, environmental samples and sites, by season) is written to `tables/T1_sample_summary.csv`.

**Not produced here:** the genomics figures from the HPC pipeline (ASA3P, FastANI, Gubbins, Roary). The Mashtree tree is drawn as Figure 9 when its file is present.

**Random numbers:** all tests are exact; the only random element is the jitter of points in Figure 8A (fixed seed).

# Setup

```{r packages}
required_pkgs <- c(
  "readxl", "tidyverse", "lubridate", "broom", "brglm2", "geepack",
  "patchwork", "ragg", "maps", "scales", "ggtext", "systemfonts", "svglite",
  "knitr", "writexl", "ape", "survey"
)
missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[!required_pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
# maps, systemfonts, svglite, ape and survey are called with :: and not attached (maps::map() would mask purrr::map()).
for (pkg in setdiff(required_pkgs, c("maps", "systemfonts", "svglite", "ape", "survey"))) library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
```

## Output directories and save helpers

```{r output-dirs}
out_dir <- "outputs"
fig_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "figures")
tab_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "tables")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(tab_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!dir.exists(fig_dir) || !dir.exists(tab_dir)) {
  stop(sprintf("Could not create output directories under '%s' (working directory: %s). Check write permissions.",
               out_dir, getwd()))
}
cat(sprintf("Output directory ready:\n  Figures -> %s\n  Tables  -> %s\n",
            normalizePath(fig_dir), normalizePath(tab_dir)))

# Write each table to CSV and keep it for the combined workbook (sheet names: 31 characters at most).
all_tables <- list()
sheet_src  <- character()
save_table <- function(df, name) {
  readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(df), file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")))
  sheet <- substr(name, 1, 31)
  if (sheet %in% names(sheet_src) && sheet_src[[sheet]] != name) {
    i <- 2
    repeat {
      sheet <- paste0(substr(name, 1, 28), "_", i)
      if (!sheet %in% names(sheet_src)) break
      i <- i + 1
    }
  }
  sheet_src[[sheet]] <<- name
  all_tables[[sheet]] <<- df
  invisible(df)
}
write_tab <- function(df, name) { save_table(df, name); invisible(df) }
```
## Data folder

Input files are read from one folder (`data_dir`, or the environment variable `SRP_DATA_DIR`).

```{r data-dir}
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("SRP_DATA_DIR", unset = "data")

required_files <- c(
  "SRP_inspection_stems_summer_2026_Prihatna.xlsx",  # 2026 stem-level data
  "SRP_inspection_stem_2025_Prihatna.xlsx",          # 2025 sample-level data
  "blackleg_2024-2025_fig.xlsx",                     # 2024 counts (sheets 2024, gen_2024, region_2024)
  "irrigating_water_2025.xlsx", "irrigating_water_2026.xlsx",
  "air_2025.xlsx", "air_2026.xlsx",
  "ani_pathogenicity.xlsx",                          # isolates: ANI and decayed tissue weight
  "pathogenicity_secretome_matrix_25.xlsx",          # PCWDE gene counts, effector candidate flag (25 isolates)
  "env_vs_plant_metadata_correlated.xlsx",           # key to the isolate codes, source class
  "ani_pitting.xlsx",                                 # pitting on CVP agar (the isolate table plus a Pitting column)
  "name_crosswalks.csv"                              # grower name mappings (private, not in the repository)
)
# Optional (the matching figure or check is skipped when absent): effector_candidates_25.xlsx, Table2_isolate_source_qpcr_pitting.csv, Table4_isolate_ani_taxonomy_source.csv.
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) {
  stop(sprintf("Data folder not found: %s. Set `data_dir` or the environment variable SRP_DATA_DIR.", data_dir))
}
absent <- required_files[!file.exists(file.path(data_dir, required_files))]
if (length(absent) > 0) stop("Missing input file(s) in ", data_dir, ": ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "))
cat("All", length(required_files), "input files found in", data_dir, "\n")
```

## Shared helpers and constants

```{r helpers}
# Date parsing that tolerates mixed formats.
safe_parse_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXct")) return(as.Date(x))

  x_chr <- str_trim(as.character(x))
  parsed <- rep(as.Date(NA), length(x_chr))

  is_serial <- str_detect(x_chr, "^[0-9]{4,6}(\\.[0-9]+)?$") & !is.na(x_chr)
  if (any(is_serial)) {
    parsed[is_serial] <- as.Date(as.numeric(x_chr[is_serial]), origin = "1899-12-30")
  }

  remaining <- !is_serial & !is.na(x_chr) & x_chr != ""
  if (any(remaining)) {
    parsed[remaining] <- suppressWarnings(
      lubridate::parse_date_time(
        x_chr[remaining],
        orders = c("Ymd HMS", "Ymd", "mdy HM", "mdy", "dmy", "m/d/Y", "m/d/y", "Y/m/d")
      )
    ) %>% as.Date()
  }
  parsed
}

pathogen_labels <- c(
  pectobacterium_spp = "Pectobacterium spp.",
  p_atrosepticum      = "P. atrosepticum",
  dickeya_spp         = "Dickeya spp.",
  d_dianthicola       = "D. dianthicola"
)
detect_cols <- names(pathogen_labels)
any_cols    <- paste0("any_", detect_cols)
n_pos_cols  <- paste0("n_pos_", detect_cols)

# Names used by the statistics and figure code below.
targets <- pathogen_labels
keys    <- names(targets)
anyc    <- any_cols
npc     <- n_pos_cols

# Exact (Clopper-Pearson) interval on the proportion scale (0-1) and on the percent scale (0-100).
cp_prop <- function(x, n) { ci <- binom.test(x, n)$conf.int; c(lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2]) }
cp_pct  <- function(x, n) { ci <- binom.test(x, n)$conf.int; c(lo = 100 * ci[1], hi = 100 * ci[2]) }
```
## Figure style

Season colours: 2024 blue, 2025 orange, 2026 green (colour-vision-deficiency safe). Font: Arial, falling back to Helvetica or Liberation Sans (metrically identical to Arial). All figure text is black; all text sizes are multiplied by `font_scale`.

```{r figure-style}
fonts_available <- systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
fam <- intersect(c("Arial", "Helvetica", "Liberation Sans"), fonts_available)[1]
if (is.na(fam)) fam <- "sans"
cat("Figure font:", fam, "\n")

yr_col  <- c("2024" = "#2a78d6", "2025" = "#eb6834", "2026" = "#1baf7a")
gen_col <- c("Pectobacterium only" = "#4a3aa7", "Dickeya only" = "#eda100", "Both genera" = "#e34948", "Neither" = "#cfcec8")
ink <- "#1f1f1d"; ink2 <- "#52514e"; ink3 <- "#8a8984"; surf <- "#f3f2ee"
ink_t <- "#000000"   # colour of all text in the figures
font_scale <- 1.3            # text scale for the figures (every font size in the figure code is multiplied by this)
blue_ramp <- c("#eef4fc", "#9ec5f4", "#3987e5", "#184f95", "#0d366b")

# Italic species names via markdown (ggtext); "spp." stays upright.
target_md <- c(pectobacterium_spp = "<i>Pectobacterium</i> spp.",
               p_atrosepticum     = "<i>P. atrosepticum</i>",
               dickeya_spp        = "<i>Dickeya</i> spp.",
               d_dianthicola      = "<i>D. dianthicola</i>")
lab_target <- as_labeller(target_md)
tgt_fac <- function(x) factor(x, levels = keys)

theme_ms <- function(bs = 10) {
  bs <- bs * font_scale
  theme_classic(base_size = bs, base_family = fam) +
    theme(text = element_text(colour = ink_t), axis.text = element_text(colour = ink_t),
          axis.line = element_line(linewidth = .4, colour = ink2), axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = .4, colour = ink2),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = surf, colour = NA), strip.text = element_markdown(face = "bold", size = bs, colour = ink_t),
          axis.text.x = element_markdown(colour = ink_t), axis.text.y = element_markdown(colour = ink_t),
          legend.key.size = unit(.9 * font_scale, "lines"), legend.text = element_text(size = bs - font_scale), legend.title = element_text(size = bs, face = "bold"),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = bs + 3 * font_scale), plot.margin = margin(6, 8, 6, 6),
          panel.spacing = unit(.9, "lines"))
}

# Save one figure as PNG (300 dpi, ragg), PDF (vector, fonts embedded) and SVG (editable text), white background.
save_ms <- function(p, name, w, h) {
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 300, device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white")
  pdf_dev <- if (isTRUE(capabilities("cairo"))) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h, device = pdf_dev, bg = "white")
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".svg")), p, width = w, height = h, device = svglite::svglite, bg = "white")
  cat("saved", name, "(", w, "x", h, "in )\n")
  invisible(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".png")))
}
# Show the saved PNG in the knitted report, so the report displays the exact file.
show_fig <- function(name) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".png")))

# ANI tier labels (the label contains the "greater than or equal" sign, built here so the code stays ASCII).
tier_hi <- paste0("ANI ", intToUtf8(0x2265), " 95%")
tier_lo <- "ANI < 95%"

pct_lab  <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", x)
pct_num  <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x)   # bar labels where the bars are narrow; the axis title gives the unit
tag_wrap <- function(p) p + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & theme(plot.tag.position = c(0, 1), plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13 * font_scale, family = fam, colour = ink_t))
```
# Data cleaning

Produces `stem_df` (2026, one row per stem) and `sample_all` (2025 and 2026, one row per sample). The 2024 season (counts per sample only) is added later from its own workbook.

# Data import: 2026 season (stem-level)

## Read and rename

```{r file-path-2026}
data_path_2026 <- file.path(data_dir, "SRP_inspection_stems_summer_2026_Prihatna.xlsx")
sheet_2026     <- "Inspector Samples"
readxl::excel_sheets(data_path_2026)
```

```{r read-2026}
raw2026 <- read_excel(data_path_2026, sheet = sheet_2026)
glimpse(raw2026)
```

```{r rename-2026}
df2026 <- raw2026 %>%
  rename(
    sample_num                = `Sample #`,
    code                      = Codes,
    n_samples_declared        = `# of Samples`,
    grower                    = Grower,
    region                    = Region,
    field                     = Field,
    acres                     = Acres,
    generation                = Gen,
    variety                   = Variety,
    seed_lot_id               = `Seed Lot ID`,
    lat                       = Lat,
    long                      = Long,
    date_sampled              = `Date Sampled`,
    date_tested               = `Date Tested`,
    date_recorded             = `Date Recorded`,
    n_positive_dickeya_legacy = `# Positive (Dickeya)`,
    pectobacterium_spp        = `Pectobacterium spp.`,
    p_atrosepticum            = `P. atrosepticum`,
    dickeya_spp                = `Dickeya spp.`,
    d_dianthicola               = `D. dianthicola`
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(detect_cols), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))))
```

## Parse dates and trim the valid stem-level block

```{r parse-dates-2026}
date_cols_2026 <- c("date_sampled", "date_tested", "date_recorded")
n_unparsed_2026 <- df2026 %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(date_cols_2026), ~ sum(!is.na(.) & is.na(safe_parse_date(.))))) %>%
  unlist()

df2026 <- df2026 %>% mutate(across(all_of(date_cols_2026), safe_parse_date))

if (any(n_unparsed_2026 > 0)) {
  cat("2026: some date entries could not be parsed and were set to NA:\n")
  print(n_unparsed_2026[n_unparsed_2026 > 0])
} else {
  cat("2026: all date entries parsed successfully.\n")
}
```
Keep the stem-level block: rows above the first row with all four pathogen columns missing.

```{r trim-2026}
row_flags_2026 <- df2026 %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number(),
         n_present = rowSums(!is.na(across(all_of(detect_cols)))))

first_blank_2026 <- row_flags_2026 %>% filter(n_present == 0) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(row_id)
if (length(first_blank_2026) == 0) first_blank_2026 <- nrow(df2026) + 1

stem_raw_2026 <- df2026 %>% slice(1:(first_blank_2026 - 1))

cat(sprintf(
  "2026: kept rows 1-%d as the valid stem-level record block (dropped %d trailing rows).\n",
  first_blank_2026 - 1, nrow(df2026) - (first_blank_2026 - 1)
))
```
## Forward-fill sample-level metadata, drop empty columns, clean placeholders

Sample-level fields are entered on the first stem row only and are filled down to all stems of the sample.

```{r forward-fill-2026}
sample_level_cols_2026 <- c(
  "sample_num", "n_samples_declared", "grower", "region", "field", "acres",
  "generation", "variety", "seed_lot_id", "date_sampled", "date_tested",
  "date_recorded"
)

stem_df <- stem_raw_2026 %>%
  tidyr::fill(all_of(sample_level_cols_2026), .direction = "down") %>%
  mutate(sample_id = factor(sample_num))
```

```{r drop-empty-2026}
completeness_2026 <- stem_df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(!is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "pct_complete") %>%
  arrange(pct_complete)

save_table(completeness_2026, "column_completeness_2026")
kable(completeness_2026, digits = 2, caption = "2026: column completeness in the trimmed stem-level block")

cols_to_drop_2026 <- completeness_2026 %>% filter(pct_complete < 0.10) %>% pull(column)
cat("2026: dropping columns with <10% completeness:", paste(cols_to_drop_2026, collapse = ", "), "\n")
stem_df <- stem_df %>% select(-all_of(cols_to_drop_2026))
```

```{r clean-placeholders-2026}
stem_df <- stem_df %>%
  mutate(
    grower  = str_trim(grower),
    variety = str_trim(variety),
    grower  = na_if(grower, "TBD"),
    variety = na_if(variety, "TBD"),
    generation = as.character(generation),
    generation = if_else(is.na(generation), NA_character_, paste0("G", generation))
  )
```
`stem_df` is the cleaned 2026 stem-level dataset (n = `r nrow(stem_df)` stems in `r n_distinct(stem_df$sample_id)` samples).

```{r read-rename-2025}
glimpse(raw2025)

    sample_num                = `Sample #`,
    grower                    = Grower,
    region                    = Region,

    acres                     = Acres,
```

## Parse dates, clean placeholder values, and validate the count logic

```{r clean-2025}
date_cols_2025 <- c("date_sampled", "date_tested", "date_recorded")
n_unparsed_2025 <- df2025 %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(date_cols_2025), ~ sum(!is.na(.) & is.na(safe_parse_date(.))))) %>%
  unlist()
df2025 <- df2025 %>% mutate(across(all_of(date_cols_2025), safe_parse_date))
if (any(n_unparsed_2025 > 0)) {
  cat("2025: some date entries could not be parsed and were set to NA:\n")
  print(n_unparsed_2025[n_unparsed_2025 > 0])
} else {
  cat("2025: all date entries parsed successfully.\n")
}

df2025 <- df2025 %>%
  mutate(
    grower = str_trim(grower),
    field  = na_if(str_trim(as.character(field)), "-"),
    acres  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(na_if(as.character(acres), "-"))),
    variety = str_trim(variety),
    generation = str_trim(generation)
  )

# Flag any row where a positive count exceeds the number of stems tested (data-entry error).
count_violations_2025 <- df2025 %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(n_pos_cols), ~ . > n_stems)) %>%
  select(sample_num, grower, n_stems, all_of(n_pos_cols))

save_table(count_violations_2025, "count_logic_violations_2025")
if (nrow(count_violations_2025) == 0) {
  cat("2025: no rows where a pathogen's positive count exceeds stems tested -- count logic is internally consistent.\n")
} else {
  kable(count_violations_2025, caption = "2025: rows where a positive count exceeds stems tested (data-entry error)")
}
```
`df2025` has the same "positives out of N stems" resolution as the aggregated 2026 data.

# Harmonizing and combining the two seasons

## Name crosswalks

Grower and variety names are harmonized across seasons with high-confidence mappings (grower mappings in `name_crosswalks.csv`); ambiguous cases are listed in a table.

```{r crosswalks}
xw <- readr::read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "name_crosswalks.csv"), col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"), na = character())
xw_map <- function(s) { d <- xw[xw$set == s, ]; setNames(d$standard, d$raw) }
grower_crosswalk <- xw_map("grower")
placeholder_growers <- xw$raw[xw$set == "placeholder_grower"]

variety_crosswalk <- c(
  "Alt"             = "Alturas",         # 2026 abbreviation -> 2025 full name
  "Burbank"         = "Russet Burbank",  # 2025 short form -> standardized full name
  "Russett Burbank" = "Russet Burbank",  # 2026 spelling (extra "t") -> standardized
  "Ranger"          = "Russet Ranger",   # 2025 short form -> standardized full name
  "Russett Ranger"  = "Russet Ranger"    # 2026 spelling (extra "t") -> standardized
)
placeholder_varieties <- c("TBD")

harmonize_grower <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(x)
  x <- recode(x, !!!grower_crosswalk)
  if_else(x %in% placeholder_growers, NA_character_, x)
}
harmonize_variety <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(x)
  x <- recode(x, !!!variety_crosswalk)
  if_else(x %in% placeholder_varieties, NA_character_, x)
}

crosswalk_applied <- tibble(
  raw_name = c(names(grower_crosswalk), names(variety_crosswalk)),
  standardized_to = c(unname(grower_crosswalk), unname(variety_crosswalk)),
  type = c(rep("grower", length(grower_crosswalk)), rep("variety", length(variety_crosswalk)))
)
save_table(crosswalk_applied, "name_harmonization_crosswalk_applied")
kable(crosswalk_applied, caption = "Name harmonization automatically applied across the two seasons")

ambiguous_names <- xw %>% filter(set == "ambiguous") %>%
  transmute(name = raw, possibly_related_to = standard, note = "Kept as a separate category; merge not confirmed")
save_table(ambiguous_names, "names_flagged_not_merged")
kable(ambiguous_names, caption = "Names that look potentially related across records but were NOT auto-merged")
```

## Aggregate 2026 up to the sample level, and finalize 2025

```{r aggregate-2026}
sample_2026 <- stem_df %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    sample_num    = as.character(first(sample_num)),
    grower        = first(grower),
    variety       = first(variety),
    generation    = first(generation),
    field         = first(field),
    acres         = first(acres),
    date_sampled  = first(date_sampled),
    date_tested   = if ("date_tested" %in% names(stem_df)) first(date_tested) else as.Date(NA),
    date_recorded = if ("date_recorded" %in% names(stem_df)) first(date_recorded) else as.Date(NA),
    n_stems       = n(),
    across(all_of(detect_cols), ~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "n_pos_{.col}"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year          = 2026L,
    region        = NA_character_,
    seed_lot_id   = NA_character_,
    lat           = NA_real_,
    long          = NA_real_,
    sample_uid    = paste0("2026_", sample_num)
  )

sample_2025 <- df2025 %>%
  mutate(
    sample_num = as.character(sample_num),
    year       = 2025L,
    sample_uid = paste0("2025_", sample_num)
  ) %>%
  select(-n_positive_dickeya_legacy)

common_cols <- c("sample_uid", "year", "sample_num", "grower", "region", "field", "acres",
                  "generation", "variety", "seed_lot_id", "lat", "long",
                  "date_sampled", "date_tested", "date_recorded",
                  "n_stems", n_pos_cols)

sample_all <- bind_rows(
  sample_2025 %>% select(all_of(common_cols)),
  sample_2026 %>% select(all_of(common_cols))
) %>%
  mutate(
    grower     = harmonize_grower(grower),
    variety    = harmonize_variety(variety),
    across(all_of(n_pos_cols), ~ as.integer(.))
  )

# Binary "any positive" indicators from the counts.
sample_all <- sample_all %>%
  mutate(
    any_pectobacterium_spp = as.integer(n_pos_pectobacterium_spp > 0),
    any_p_atrosepticum      = as.integer(n_pos_p_atrosepticum > 0),
    any_dickeya_spp         = as.integer(n_pos_dickeya_spp > 0),
    any_d_dianthicola       = as.integer(n_pos_d_dianthicola > 0)
  )

# One ordered generation factor across seasons (2025 includes G1).
gen_levels <- sample_all$generation %>% na.omit() %>% unique() %>%
  str_remove("^G") %>% as.integer() %>% sort() %>% paste0("G", .)
sample_all <- sample_all %>%
  mutate(generation = factor(generation, levels = gen_levels, ordered = TRUE))

cat(sprintf(
  "Combined dataset: %d samples (%d in 2025, %d in 2026), %d total stems tested.\n",
  nrow(sample_all), sum(sample_all$year == 2025), sum(sample_all$year == 2026), sum(sample_all$n_stems)
))
```

## Infer 2026 Region and GPS coordinates from matched 2025 growers

Region and centroid coordinates of 2026 samples are taken from the matched grower's 2025 fields (keyword-based matching); coordinates are approximate (`max_spread_km` per grower).

```{r region-coord-crosswalk}
# Broader, keyword-based grower matching used only to impute location; keyword-only matches are flagged lower confidence.
region_coord_crosswalk <- xw_map("region_coord")
low_confidence_sources <- xw$raw[xw$set == "region_coord" & xw$low_confidence == "yes"]

# Flat-earth distance approximation (adequate at tens of km; no geospatial package needed).
approx_km <- function(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
  mean_lat <- (lat1 + lat2) / 2 * pi / 180
  sqrt(((lat1 - lat2) * 111)^2 + ((lon1 - lon2) * 111 * cos(mean_lat))^2)
}

grower_fields_2025 <- sample_2025 %>%
  filter(!grower %in% placeholder_growers) %>%
  mutate(
    grower_h = recode(grower, !!!region_coord_crosswalk),
    low_confidence = grower %in% low_confidence_sources
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(grower_h))

grower_location_lookup <- grower_fields_2025 %>%
  group_by(grower_h) %>%
  summarise(
    region = if (n_distinct(na.omit(region)) == 1) first(na.omit(region)) else NA_character_,
    lat_centroid    = mean(lat, na.rm = TRUE),
    long_centroid   = mean(long, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_source_fields = n_distinct(paste(lat, long)[!is.na(lat) & !is.na(long)]),
    any_low_confidence_source = any(low_confidence),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

field_spread <- grower_fields_2025 %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(long)) %>%
  distinct(grower_h, lat, long) %>%
  left_join(grower_location_lookup %>% select(grower_h, lat_centroid, long_centroid), by = "grower_h") %>%
  mutate(dist_km = approx_km(lat_centroid, long_centroid, lat, long)) %>%
  group_by(grower_h) %>%
  summarise(max_spread_km = round(max(dist_km), 1), .groups = "drop")

grower_location_lookup <- grower_location_lookup %>%
  left_join(field_spread, by = "grower_h") %>%
  mutate(
    max_spread_km = replace_na(max_spread_km, 0),
    match_basis = if_else(any_low_confidence_source,
                           "keyword match (lower confidence)",
                           "harmonized/exact name match")
  ) %>%
  select(grower_h, region, lat_centroid, long_centroid, n_source_fields, max_spread_km, match_basis) %>%
  arrange(grower_h)

save_table(grower_location_lookup, "grower_region_coordinate_lookup")
kable(grower_location_lookup, digits = 4,
      caption = "Region and centroid GPS coordinates inferred per grower from 2025 field records (max_spread_km = distance of that grower's furthest known field from the centroid)")
```

```{r apply-region-coord-imputation}
sample_all <- sample_all %>%
  left_join(
    grower_location_lookup %>%
      select(grower = grower_h, region_inferred = region, lat_inferred = lat_centroid,
             long_inferred = long_centroid, max_spread_km),
    by = "grower"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    coordinate_source = case_when(
      year == 2025 & !is.na(lat) ~ "Recorded directly (2025)",
      year == 2026 & !is.na(lat_inferred) ~ "Inferred from matched grower's 2025 fields",
      TRUE ~ "Not available"
    ),
    region = if_else(is.na(region), region_inferred, region),
    lat    = if_else(is.na(lat), lat_inferred, lat),
    long   = if_else(is.na(long), long_inferred, long)
  ) %>%
  select(-region_inferred, -lat_inferred, -long_inferred)

n_2026_matched   <- sample_all %>% filter(year == 2026, coordinate_source != "Not available") %>% nrow()
n_2026_unmatched <- sample_all %>% filter(year == 2026, coordinate_source == "Not available") %>% nrow()
cat(sprintf(
  "2026: %d of %d samples got Region/coordinates inferred from a matched grower; %d could not be matched (grower not present in 2025 under any recognized name/keyword).\n",
  n_2026_matched, n_2026_matched + n_2026_unmatched, n_2026_unmatched
))

unmatched_2026_growers <- sample_all %>%
  filter(year == 2026, coordinate_source == "Not available") %>%
  distinct(grower)
if (nrow(unmatched_2026_growers) > 0) {
  save_table(unmatched_2026_growers, "unmatched_2026_growers_no_coordinates")
  kable(unmatched_2026_growers, caption = "2026 growers with no 2025 counterpart -- Region/coordinates could not be inferred for these")
}
```

# 2024 season and the three-season sample-level table

2024 is read from the count sheets of `blackleg_2024-2025_fig.xlsx` (`2024`, `gen_2024`, `region_2024`), so all percentages are computed here. The three sheets list the same 85 samples in different row orders: the overall and generation sheets are matched by row (checked below); the region sheet is used for region analyses only.

```{r read-2024}
rename_targets <- function(df) {
  nm <- names(df); norm <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(nm)); key <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(targets))
  names(df)[match(key, norm)] <- keys; df
}

# ---- 2024 (blackleg_2024-2025_fig.xlsx) --------------------------------------
f24  <- file.path(data_dir, "blackleg_2024-2025_fig.xlsx")
o24  <- read_excel(f24, "2024")      %>% drop_na(Sample) %>% rename_targets()
g24  <- read_excel(f24, "gen_2024")  %>% filter(!is.na(Generation)) %>% rename_targets()
r24  <- read_excel(f24, "region_2024") %>% filter(!is.na(region)) %>% rename_targets()
stopifnot(nrow(o24) == nrow(g24), all((o24[keys] > 0) == (g24[keys] > 0)))   # sheets describe the same 85 samples
```
`S` is the sample-level table for all three seasons; `SR` is the region table (the 2024 region sheet plus the 2025 and 2026 samples with a region).

```{r sample-tables}
# sample-level table, all three seasons ----------------------------------------
s24 <- tibble(year = 2024L, sample_id = paste0("2024_", o24$Sample),
              region = NA_character_, generation = toupper(trimws(g24$Generation)),
              variety = NA_character_, n_stems = g24$`sample number`) %>%
  bind_cols(setNames(as_tibble(g24[keys]),  npc)) %>%
  bind_cols(setNames(as_tibble((o24[keys] > 0) * 1L), anyc))

s2526 <- sample_all %>%
  transmute(year = as.integer(year), sample_id = sample_uid, region, generation = as.character(generation), variety, n_stems,
            across(all_of(npc)), across(all_of(anyc)), lat, long)
S <- bind_rows(s24, s2526) %>% mutate(year = factor(year, levels = 2024:2026))

# 2024 region sheet (separate row order; used for region analyses only)
R24 <- r24 %>% transmute(year = 2024L, region = trimws(region), n_stems = `sample number`,
                         across(all_of(keys), ~ as.integer(. > 0), .names = "any_{.col}"),
                         across(all_of(keys), ~ as.integer(.), .names = "n_pos_{.col}"))
SR <- bind_rows(R24 %>% mutate(sample_id = paste0("2024r_", row_number())),
                s2526 %>% filter(!is.na(region)) %>% select(year, region, n_stems, all_of(anyc), all_of(npc), sample_id)) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year, levels = 2024:2026))

cat("Samples per year:\n"); print(table(S$year))
cat("Stems per year  :\n"); print(tapply(S$n_stems, S$year, sum))
cat("Region sheet 2024 P. atro (any) =", sum(R24$any_p_atrosepticum), " vs overall sheet =", sum(o24$p_atrosepticum > 0), "\n")
```
# Environmental surveillance data: air and irrigation water

Air and irrigation water were sampled in 2025 and 2026. Regions are assigned by GPS proximity to the 2025 stem-based region centroids, not by site name.

## Data import

### Irrigation water (both years)

Both water files have one row per test, with `Sample` (site) and `Rep` (replicate) columns.

```{r file-path-env}
data_path_water_2025 <- file.path(data_dir, "irrigating_water_2025.xlsx")
data_path_water_2026 <- file.path(data_dir, "irrigating_water_2026.xlsx")
data_path_air_2025   <- file.path(data_dir, "air_2025.xlsx")
data_path_air_2026   <- file.path(data_dir, "air_2026.xlsx")

raw_water_2025 <- read_excel(data_path_water_2025, sheet = "Sheet1")
raw_water_2026 <- read_excel(data_path_water_2026, sheet = "Sheet1")
glimpse(raw_water_2025)
```
### Air (both years) -- one file has a stacked, multi-block layout

`air_2026.xlsx` contains two stacked "enrichment replicate" blocks; the parser splits them and reads a single block as is (`air_2025.xlsx`).

```{r parse-stacked-blocks-fn}
# Split the sheet into blocks at "enrichment replicate N" label rows; plain read (replicate = 1) when no label exists.
parse_stacked_replicate_blocks <- function(path, sheet = "Sheet1") {
  raw  <- read_excel(path, sheet = sheet, col_names = FALSE)
  col1 <- as.character(raw[[1]])

  block_starts <- which(str_detect(str_to_lower(coalesce(col1, "")), "enrichment replicate"))

  if (length(block_starts) == 0) {
    return(read_excel(path, sheet = sheet) %>% mutate(replicate = 1L))
  }

  block_ends <- c(block_starts[-1] - 1, nrow(raw))

  map2_dfr(block_starts, block_ends, function(start_row, end_row) {
    replicate_num <- as.integer(str_extract(col1[start_row], "[0-9]+"))
    header_row <- start_row + 1
    data_start <- start_row + 2
    if (data_start > end_row) return(tibble())
    block_data <- raw[data_start:end_row, ]
    names(block_data) <- unlist(raw[header_row, ], use.names = FALSE)
    block_data <- block_data[!is.na(block_data[[1]]), ]  # plain base-R row filter, not a dplyr .data lookup
    block_data %>%
      mutate(across(c(Lat, Long, `Pectobacterium spp.`, `P. atrosepticum`,
                       `Dickeya spp.`, `D. dianthicola`), as.numeric)) %>%
      mutate(replicate = replicate_num)
  })
}

raw_air_2025 <- parse_stacked_replicate_blocks(data_path_air_2025)
raw_air_2026 <- parse_stacked_replicate_blocks(data_path_air_2026)

cat(sprintf("air_2025: %d rows read, %d enrichment replicate block(s) detected.\n",
            nrow(raw_air_2025), n_distinct(raw_air_2025$replicate)))
cat(sprintf("air_2026: %d rows read, %d enrichment replicate block(s) detected.\n",
            nrow(raw_air_2026), n_distinct(raw_air_2026$replicate)))
```
## Harmonize columns

Columns are renamed by name, not position. Replicate numbers for air come from the parser (2026) or from repeated Name/Lat/Long rows (2025).

```{r rename-env-cols}
rename_env_cols <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    rename(
      lat = Lat,
      long = Long,
      pectobacterium_spp = `Pectobacterium spp.`,
      p_atrosepticum      = `P. atrosepticum`,
      dickeya_spp         = `Dickeya spp.`,
      d_dianthicola        = `D. dianthicola`
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(lat, long, all_of(detect_cols)), as.numeric))
}

water_2025 <- raw_water_2025 %>% rename_env_cols() %>%
  mutate(sample_type = "Water", year = 2025L, site_key = paste0("W2025_S", Sample),
         replicate = Rep) %>%
  select(sample_type, year, site_key, replicate, lat, long, all_of(detect_cols))
water_2026 <- raw_water_2026 %>% rename_env_cols() %>%
  mutate(sample_type = "Water", year = 2026L, site_key = paste0("W2026_S", Sample),
         replicate = Rep) %>%
  select(sample_type, year, site_key, replicate, lat, long, all_of(detect_cols))
air_2025 <- raw_air_2025 %>% rename_env_cols() %>%
  mutate(sample_type = "Air", year = 2025L,
         site_key = paste0("A2025_", round(lat, 5), "_", round(long, 5))) %>%
  select(sample_type, year, site_key, replicate, lat, long, all_of(detect_cols))
air_2026 <- raw_air_2026 %>% rename_env_cols() %>%
  mutate(sample_type = "Air", year = 2026L,
         site_key = paste0("A2026_", round(lat, 5), "_", round(long, 5))) %>%
  select(sample_type, year, site_key, replicate, lat, long, all_of(detect_cols))

env_raw <- bind_rows(water_2025, water_2026, air_2025, air_2026)
```
Positive longitudes are converted to negative (western hemisphere).

```{r fix-longitude-sign}
long_sign_fixed <- env_raw %>% filter(long > 0)
if (nrow(long_sign_fixed) > 0) {
  save_table(long_sign_fixed %>% select(sample_type, year, site_key, lat, long),
             "environmental_longitude_sign_corrections")
  cat(sprintf("Corrected %d row(s) with a positive longitude (missing minus sign):\n", nrow(long_sign_fixed)))
  print(long_sign_fixed %>% select(sample_type, year, site_key, long))
} else {
  cat("No longitude sign issues detected.\n")
}
env_raw <- env_raw %>% mutate(long = if_else(long > 0, -abs(long), long))
```
## Aggregate replicate-level tests up to one row per site

Replicate tests are aggregated to one row per site (`n_tests` corresponds to `n_stems`).

```{r aggregate-env-sites}
env_sites <- env_raw %>%
  group_by(sample_type, year, site_key) %>%
  summarise(
    lat = first(lat),
    long = first(long),
    n_tests = n(),
    across(all_of(detect_cols), ~ sum(. == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "n_pos_{.col}"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    any_pectobacterium_spp = as.integer(n_pos_pectobacterium_spp > 0),
    any_p_atrosepticum      = as.integer(n_pos_p_atrosepticum > 0),
    any_dickeya_spp         = as.integer(n_pos_dickeya_spp > 0),
    any_d_dianthicola       = as.integer(n_pos_d_dianthicola > 0)
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "%d environmental sites total: %d Water (%d in 2025, %d in 2026), %d Air (%d in 2025, %d in 2026).\n",
  nrow(env_sites),
  sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Water"), sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Water" & env_sites$year == 2025),
  sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Water" & env_sites$year == 2026),
  sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Air"), sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Air" & env_sites$year == 2025),
  sum(env_sites$sample_type == "Air" & env_sites$year == 2026)
))
```
## Assign region by GPS proximity (not by name)

Each site is assigned to the nearest region centroid (from directly recorded 2025 stem coordinates), with the same distance approximation as above.

```{r assign-env-region}
region_centroids <- sample_all %>%
  filter(year == 2025, !is.na(region), !is.na(lat), !is.na(long)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(centroid_lat = mean(lat), centroid_long = mean(long), .groups = "drop")

env_sites <- env_sites %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    region_dist_km = round(min(approx_km(lat, long, region_centroids$centroid_lat, region_centroids$centroid_long)), 1),
    region = region_centroids$region[which.min(approx_km(lat, long, region_centroids$centroid_lat, region_centroids$centroid_long))]
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

save_table(
  env_sites %>% select(sample_type, year, site_key, lat, long, region, region_dist_km),
  "environmental_region_assignment"
)
kable(env_sites %>% select(sample_type, year, site_key, region, region_dist_km),
      caption = "Region assigned to each environmental site by nearest GPS centroid (region_dist_km = distance to that region's centroid, from 2025 stem data)")

far_sites <- env_sites %>% filter(region_dist_km > 50)
if (nrow(far_sites) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Note: %d site(s) are >50 km from their nearest region centroid -- check whether these lie outside the three known regions:\n", nrow(far_sites)))
  print(far_sites %>% select(sample_type, year, site_key, region, region_dist_km))
}

save_table(env_sites, "cleaned_environmental_site_data_both_years")
```
# Isolate WGS identity vs. decayed tissue weight (pathogenicity assay)

Isolates (`ani_pathogenicity.xlsx`) were cultured from samples and sequenced; `WGS status/ANI` and `ID (based on ANI)` give the species call. Decayed tissue weight comes from a tuber maceration assay on a subset.

## Data import

```{r file-path-isolates}
data_path_isolates <- file.path(data_dir, "ani_pathogenicity.xlsx")
readxl::excel_sheets(data_path_isolates)
```

```{r read-clean-isolates}
raw_isolates <- read_excel(data_path_isolates, sheet = "Sheet1")

isolates <- raw_isolates %>%
  transmute(
    isolate_code = `Isolate code`,
    wgs_ani_raw  = `WGS status/ANI`,
    id_ani       = `ID (based on ANI)`,
    decay_g      = `decayed tissue weight`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Numeric %ANI and text flags (e.g. "outlier") share one column.
    ani_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wgs_ani_raw)),
    wgs_status  = case_when(
      is.na(wgs_ani_raw)  ~ "No ANI result",   # never sent, or sent without a result
      !is.na(ani_numeric) ~ "ANI resolved",
      TRUE                ~ str_to_sentence(as.character(wgs_ani_raw))
    ),
    genus = case_when(
      str_starts(id_ani, "Dickeya")        ~ "Dickeya",
      str_starts(id_ani, "Pectobacterium") ~ "Pectobacterium",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

save_table(isolates, "isolate_wgs_ani_decay_data")
cat(sprintf(
  "Isolates: %d total, %d with a WGS-based species ID, %d with decayed tissue weight measured, %d with both.\n",
  nrow(isolates), sum(!is.na(isolates$id_ani)), sum(!is.na(isolates$decay_g)),
  sum(!is.na(isolates$id_ani) & !is.na(isolates$decay_g))
))
```
## Pitting on CVP agar

`ani_pitting.xlsx` adds a `Pitting` column (crystal violet pectate agar; `-`, `+`, `++`, `+++`, coded 0-3 and treated as ordinal). Only this column is used; ANI, species and decayed tissue weight stay from `ani_pathogenicity.xlsx`. Differences between the two files are written to `T_pitting_file_discrepancies.csv` (chunk `pitting-qc`).

```{r read-pitting}
data_path_pit <- file.path(data_dir, "ani_pitting.xlsx")
pit_raw <- read_excel(data_path_pit, sheet = "Sheet1")
stopifnot("ani_pitting.xlsx needs the columns 'Isolate code' and 'Pitting'" = all(c("Isolate code", "Pitting") %in% names(pit_raw)))

pit_levels <- c("-", "+", "++", "+++")
minus <- intToUtf8(0x2212)
pit_cols <- c("-" = "#eef4fc", "+" = "#9ec5f4", "++" = "#3987e5", "+++" = "#184f95", "not tested" = "#cfcec8")   # one hue, light to dark
pit_lab  <- c("-" = minus, "+" = "+", "++" = "++", "+++" = "+++", "not tested" = "not tested")
pit_factor <- function(x) factor(ifelse(is.na(x), "not tested", x), levels = names(pit_cols))

n_nocode <- sum(is.na(pit_raw$`Isolate code`) & !is.na(pit_raw$Pitting))
if (n_nocode > 0) cat(sprintf("Note: %d row(s) with a pitting score but no isolate code are ignored.\n", n_nocode))
pit <- pit_raw %>% filter(!is.na(`Isolate code`)) %>%
  transmute(isolate_code = `Isolate code`, pit_chr = str_trim(as.character(Pitting)),
            ani_pit_file = as.character(`WGS status/ANI`), id_pit_file = as.character(`ID (based on ANI)`), decay_pit_file = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`decayed tissue weight`))) %>%
  mutate(pit_chr = ifelse(pit_chr %in% c("", "NA"), NA_character_, pit_chr), pitting = match(pit_chr, pit_levels) - 1L)
bad <- pit %>% filter(!is.na(pit_chr), is.na(pitting))
if (nrow(bad) > 0) stop("Pitting scores other than -, +, ++, +++ in ani_pitting.xlsx: ", paste(unique(bad$pit_chr), collapse = ", "))
stopifnot("duplicate isolate codes in ani_pitting.xlsx" = !anyDuplicated(pit$isolate_code))
```

```{r pitting-qc}
# Compare what the two isolate files both carry (ANI, species, decayed tissue weight)
num   <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
norm  <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_, ifelse(!is.na(num(x)), formatC(num(x), digits = 8, format = "g"), as.character(x)))
eq_na <- function(a, b) (is.na(a) & is.na(b)) | (!is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & a == b)
pit_chk <- isolates %>% select(isolate_code, wgs_ani_raw, id_ani, decay_g) %>%
  inner_join(pit %>% select(isolate_code, ani_pit_file, id_pit_file, decay_pit_file), by = "isolate_code") %>%
  mutate(ani_same   = eq_na(norm(wgs_ani_raw), norm(ani_pit_file)),
         id_same    = eq_na(as.character(id_ani), id_pit_file),
         decay_same = eq_na(round(decay_g, 6), round(decay_pit_file, 6)))
pit_diff <- pit_chk %>% filter(!ani_same | !id_same | !decay_same)
save_table(pit_diff, "T_pitting_file_discrepancies")
only_a <- setdiff(isolates$isolate_code, pit$isolate_code); only_b <- setdiff(pit$isolate_code, isolates$isolate_code)
cat(sprintf("ani_pitting.xlsx vs ani_pathogenicity.xlsx: %d isolates in both, %d differ in ANI, species or decayed tissue weight; codes only in ani_pathogenicity.xlsx: %s; only in ani_pitting.xlsx: %s.\n",
            nrow(pit_chk), nrow(pit_diff), ifelse(length(only_a) == 0, "none", paste(only_a, collapse = ", ")), ifelse(length(only_b) == 0, "none", paste(only_b, collapse = ", "))))

# The column "pitting after reviving from cryo?" of ani_pathogenicity.xlsx is not used.
if ("pitting after reviving from cryo?" %in% names(raw_isolates)) {
  cryo <- raw_isolates %>% transmute(isolate_code = `Isolate code`, pitting_after_cryo = `pitting after reviving from cryo?`) %>%
    inner_join(pit %>% select(isolate_code, pit_chr), by = "isolate_code") %>% filter(!is.na(pitting_after_cryo), !is.na(pit_chr))
  cat("Old column 'pitting after reviving from cryo?' (rows) against the CVP pitting score (columns); not used:\n")
  print(table(cryo = cryo$pitting_after_cryo, CVP_score = factor(cryo$pit_chr, pit_levels)))
  save_table(cryo, "T_pitting_cryo_column_vs_cvp_score")
}

isolates <- isolates %>% left_join(pit %>% select(isolate_code, pit_chr, pitting), by = "isolate_code")
cat(sprintf("Pitting scored for %d of %d isolates (-: %d, +: %d, ++: %d, +++: %d).\n", sum(!is.na(isolates$pitting)), nrow(isolates),
            sum(isolates$pit_chr == "-", na.rm = TRUE), sum(isolates$pit_chr == "+", na.rm = TRUE), sum(isolates$pit_chr == "++", na.rm = TRUE), sum(isolates$pit_chr == "+++", na.rm = TRUE)))
```
## Genomic features: cell-wall-degrading enzyme genes and effector candidates

`pathogenicity_secretome_matrix_25.xlsx` gives, for 25 sequenced isolates, the number of genes in three plant-cell-wall-degrading enzyme classes (PCWDE: pectin-, hemicellulose- and cellulose-like) and an `effector_candidate` flag (keyword screen of the annotation, not a prediction tool). `env_vs_plant_metadata_correlated.xlsx` links sequencing sample names to isolate codes and gives the source class. `effector_candidates_25.xlsx` (the 'yes' rows) is a cross-check only.

The matrix is the primary source. Differences from the metadata workbook are written to `T_genomic_features_file_discrepancies.csv` (chunk `feature-qc`). `total_cazymes` is not analysed (values differ between the two workbooks).

```{r read-genomic-features}
data_path_feat <- file.path(data_dir, "pathogenicity_secretome_matrix_25.xlsx")
data_path_meta <- file.path(data_dir, "env_vs_plant_metadata_correlated.xlsx")
data_path_eff  <- file.path(data_dir, "effector_candidates_25.xlsx")   # optional cross-check

feat_raw <- read_excel(data_path_feat, sheet = 1)
meta_raw <- read_excel(data_path_meta, sheet = "Matched metadata")

pcwde_cols <- c("pcwde_pectin_like", "pcwde_hemicellulose_like", "pcwde_cellulose_like")
need_feat <- c("sample_raw", "lineage", pcwde_cols, "known_effector_like_keywords", "effector_candidate", "total_cazymes", "T5aSS")
need_meta <- c("full_sample_name", "workflow_short_name", "table_pi_code", "source_class", "environment_type",
               pcwde_cols, "effector_candidate", "total_cazymes")
stopifnot("secretome matrix is missing a column" = all(need_feat %in% names(feat_raw)),
          "metadata workbook is missing a column" = all(need_meta %in% names(meta_raw)),
          "T5aSS is not coded 0/1 in the secretome matrix" = all(feat_raw$T5aSS %in% c(0, 1)))

# One row per isolate; the sequencing sample name is the key between the two workbooks.
feat_join <- feat_raw %>%
  inner_join(meta_raw %>% select(full_sample_name, isolate_short = workflow_short_name, isolate_code = table_pi_code,
                                 source_class, environment_type),
             by = c("sample_raw" = "full_sample_name"))
if (nrow(feat_join) != nrow(feat_raw) || anyDuplicated(feat_join$isolate_code) > 0) {
  stop("The secretome matrix and the metadata workbook do not match one-to-one on the sample name.")
}
cat(nrow(feat_join), "isolates in the secretome matrix, all matched to an isolate code.\n")
```

```{r feature-qc}
# Compare the values that both workbooks carry.
qc_cols <- c("total_cazymes", pcwde_cols, "effector_candidate")
disc <- map_dfr(qc_cols, function(cc) {
  tibble(isolate_code      = feat_join$isolate_code,
         column            = cc,
         secretome_matrix  = as.character(feat_join[[cc]]),

}) %>% filter(secretome_matrix != metadata_workbook | is.na(secretome_matrix) != is.na(metadata_workbook))
save_table(disc, "T_genomic_features_file_discrepancies")
cat(sprintf("Secretome matrix vs. metadata workbook: %d of %d values differ.\n", nrow(disc), nrow(feat_join) * length(qc_cols)))
print(disc %>% count(column, name = "isolates_that_differ"))

tc_m <- as.numeric(meta_raw$total_cazymes); tc_f <- as.numeric(feat_join$total_cazymes)
cat(sprintf("total_cazymes: matrix %d-%d; metadata workbook %d-%d (%d values >= 1000). Not analysed.\n",
            min(tc_f), max(tc_f), min(tc_m), max(tc_m), sum(tc_m >= 1000)))

# The effector workbook should be exactly the 'yes' rows of the matrix.
if (file.exists(data_path_eff)) {
  eff_raw <- read_excel(data_path_eff)
  same <- setequal(eff_raw$sample_raw, feat_raw$sample_raw[feat_raw$effector_candidate == "yes"])

              ifelse(same, "identical to", "DIFFERENT FROM"), sum(feat_raw$effector_candidate == "yes")))
}
```

```{r merge-genomic-features}
# One row per sequenced isolate: genomic features + ANI + decayed tissue weight; source class and environment type from the metadata workbook.
geno <- feat_join %>%
  transmute(isolate_code, lineage, source_class, environment_type,
            pectin = pcwde_pectin_like, hemicellulose = pcwde_hemicellulose_like, cellulose = pcwde_cellulose_like,

save_table(geno %>% mutate(tier = as.character(tier)), "T_genomic_features_per_isolate")
cat(sprintf("%d isolates; %d with decayed tissue weight; ANI >= 95%%: %d (%d with decay); ANI < 95%%: %d (%d with decay).\n",
            nrow(geno), sum(!is.na(geno$decay_g)), sum(geno$ani >= 95), sum(geno$ani >= 95 & !is.na(geno$decay_g)),
```
